title: A window-title tag no longer fights the page for its title
body: The init script that appends a browser's label to its window title patched Document.prototype.title's setter and observed the <head> subtree its own write mutates. Against a page that re-asserts its own title -- a bot-challenge page showing status, say -- the two ping-ponged without bound: measured at roughly 1GB/s, reaching 20GB in 140 seconds, which OOM-killed every sibling browser in the pool and then the daemon's own sessions. Raw Playwright on the same page with no init scripts stayed flat at 0.54GB, so the page was never the cause. The page is now handed back its OWN value on read while the real <title> node keeps the tag, so a page comparing document.title against what it last set finds them equal and reverts nothing. The tag stays visible everywhere it is meant to be -- window chrome, tab, browser_list, page outlines -- and invisible only to the page's own scripts, the one reader it must not provoke.

title: A credential passed to a macro no longer reaches the failure payload
body: A macro argument named like a credential (password, passphrase, secret, token, api_key, access_key, private_key, authorization, cookie, otp, and their plural and camelCase forms) is now classified at run time, and its value is scrubbed out of every diagnostic surface a failure returns before that payload leaves the process: the diagnostic bundle, the healing suggestion, the failed-request tail, the executed-action descriptors, and the recorder, which writes to disk. Scrubbing covers raw, JSON-escaped and repeatedly URL-encoded spellings of the value, so a credential laundered through an encoding is caught too.

title: Screenshots taken under a classified macro argument are refused, not scrubbed
body: A screenshot of a page a credential was typed into is a durable copy of that credential, and no text scrub can reach it. So the generic capture path is refused outright while classified arguments are in play: a composition root must install both an explicit authority flag and a handler that knows what evidence is safe to keep. The generic diagnostic producer is skipped for the same reason -- it persists raw HTML and a raw screenshot -- and the payload says so rather than silently omitting it.

title: Behavior change: more argument names are refused in a macro sink
body: The credential sink guard now uses the same vocabulary as the redactors, so it refuses names its old private table did not know -- passphrase, pw, pwd, authorization, access_key, private_key, plural forms, and any name containing pwd such as dbpwd -- when a macro expands them into a url, expression, verify_js or grabbed_predicate_js. OCTOWRIGHT_MACRO_CREDENTIAL_SINKS still defaults to block, so a macro that put {{access_key}} in a query string worked in 0.22.1 and raises now, with no config change on the operator's side. The opt-out is named in the error text and exists for exactly that case: OCTOWRIGHT_MACRO_CREDENTIAL_SINKS=allow. It also covers the one known false positive: pwd matches the shell's OLDPWD, so a parameter named oldpwd holding a directory path is refused too. Measured across a 340-macro corpus on one machine, no macro was affected -- but a newly refused macro is what a different corpus would surface first, so read this as a behavior change with an opt-out, not only as a fix.

title: The sink guard missed six credential spellings
body: The guard defaults to block, so an operator is entitled to believe a credential-named argument cannot expand into a navigation or code sink. Through 0.22.1 it silently could for several spellings. It matched on its own name table, in which auth required an underscore or end-of-string boundary -- so authorization missed -- and only api_key and apikey were listed -- so access_key and private_key missed. {{password}} in a url was refused while {{passphrase}} expanded. No macro in the measured corpus used the affected names, which makes this a latent hole rather than live exposure; it becomes exposure the day someone names a parameter passphrase.

title: The sink guard now shares the macro classifier's vocabulary
body: Through 0.22.1 the artifact redactor already knew passphrase, authorization, pw, pwd and cookie while the macro sink guard did not, so the same name could be scrubbed from an artifact and still expanded into a URL. The sink guard now delegates to the new macro argument classifier, so the two share one vocabulary: the union of what every classifier matched before unification, with a match mode declared per token -- substring for long unambiguous tokens and for pwd, whole-token for other short ones, so auth does not catch author or authority. A frozen baseline fixture asserts that no name an earlier runtime classifier called sensitive became insensitive. The artifact redactor itself is unchanged since 0.22.1 and keeps its own table, with a test asserting it never drops a name it already caught.

title: Regenerate exported scripts to pick up the wider matcher
body: An exported script carries a copy of the argument matcher, not a reference to it. Scripts exported by 0.22.1 use a narrow substring table -- password, passwd, pwd, token, secret, email, username -- and miss api_key, authorization, passphrase, private_key, cookie, otp, bearer and more. Regenerating replaces it with the shared vocabulary, stamped ARG_PRIVACY_CLASSIFIER_VERSION 4. One trade to know about: the new matcher treats email and username as whole tokens, so a concatenated name like useremail that the old substring table caught is no longer matched -- rename such parameters with a separator before regenerating. pwd stays substring-matched so the trade never applies to a credential: dbpwd is still caught. No affected name appears in the measured corpus. There is no staleness detection for exported scripts today.

title: Per-directory agent guides instead of one file to read in full
body: AGENTS.md had grown to the point where an agent reading it paid for the whole repo's conventions to learn about one directory. The directory-specific material now lives in AGENTS.md files next to the code it describes (browser_pool, cli, macros, session, tests), and the two reference tables that were never directory-scoped -- every OCTOWRIGHT_* environment variable, and the telemetry spans and metrics -- moved into docs/env-vars.md and docs/telemetry.md.
